parts.title: Summer on the Dig
parts.text: Noor had waited all year for this day. Her aunt, an archaeologist, had invited Noor and her friends Caleb and Imelda to join a summer **excavation** at the edge of a dry riverbed. Under the sand, the team believed, lay the **ruins** of a trading town forgotten for three thousand years. Each volunteer received a bucket, a soft brush, and a small digging **trowel** with a pointed blade.

parts.title: Slow and Careful
parts.text: Caleb tipped each scoop of soil into a mesh screen to **sift** out beads, bone chips, and bits of pottery. By noon he had found only one faint **vestige** of the town, a stripe of red paint on a lump of clay. Then Imelda's blade scraped something hard, and all three friends knelt to **unearth** a wide, flat stone. Carved into its surface was a single **hieroglyph**, a tiny picture of a bird.

parts.title: Beneath the Stone
parts.text: Under the stone, a narrow stairway led down to a **burial** chamber where an ancient family had been laid to rest. Noor's aunt warned them to move slowly, because the clay jars inside were **brittle** and might **crumble** at the slightest bump. In one corner sat a **cache** of tiny oil lamps, stored away and forgotten for centuries. Rows of carved symbols covered the wall, and Imelda copied them into her notebook so the team could **decipher** their message later.

parts.title: Stories in the Dust
parts.text: That night the friends sat around the campfire, sunburned and covered in dust. Noor realized that archaeology was not really about treasure. It was about listening to people from long ago and noticing the small things they left behind. She fell asleep wondering what tomorrow's digging would reveal.
